correctness.rationale: Two independent finite enumeration methods give precisely 1,728 augmented faces for the triangular prism Morse complex; an explicitly defined 18-stage matching pairs 832 covers and leaves exactly 64 critical 4-simplices. Every one of 6,624 Hasse incidences is constructed, and exhaustive directed topological sorting proves no alternating cycle. Removing the augmented empty-face pair gives one critical vertex and 64 critical 4-cells, whose attachments to a point are trivial. The resulting CW homotopy type is wedge^64 S4. The published first-iterate graph isomorphism transfers the result to M(M(boundary of a triangle)). Independent mod-two boundary ranks agree. No infinite-family conclusion is claimed.

evidence: Scoville–Zaremsky arXiv:2004.10481 supplies connectivity lower bounds for graphs from edge count and maximum degree, not a classification of their Morse-complex homotopy types.
Chari–Joswig arXiv:math/0011234 describes combinatorial Morse complexes and rooted forests, with no relevant prism homotopy theorem found.
Indexed sphere-wedge results for K_{3,3}, K_{2,n}, and K_{2,2,2} concern distinct graph inputs and do not imply a result for C_3 square K_2.

Jojić, arXiv:1109.4475v2, Theorem 15 restricts its vertex-decomposability guarantee to digraphs whose undirected support is a tree, and the complete-source shellability criterion requires a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. The bidirected prism has cycles and degree three on six vertices, so neither hypothesis holds.

value.rationale: This is a natural second iterate of the discrete Morse-complex construction on the smallest triangular cycle, rather than an arbitrary graph slice. A previous exact mod-two benchmark does not resolve integral homotopy; the explicit perfect discrete-Morse matching settles the full homotopy type and eliminates the possibility of hidden torsion or nontrivial attaching maps, giving a reproducible structural case for iterated Morse complexes.
